To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a classification scheme for quantifying low-level injuries of humans in industrial robot systems is presented; b) the classification is applicable to a wide range of industrial robot systems; and c) a prototype software tool for the quantification of low-level injuries is presented.

the injury potential of a robot can be quantified in a way that is unambiguously comparable to the quantification of the injury potential of other physical agents, and that the injury potential can be expressed in terms of the probability of causing a given type of injury.

the injury risk for industrial robots in collaborative operation with humans must be quantified and that a classification scheme for the injury risk is needed to facilitate a common language and a systematic approach to the assessment and comparison of collaborative robot designs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of methods to assess injury potential of collaborative robots.
the quantification of the injury potential of collaborative robots and systems.
the question of how to assess injury risks in a quantitative and standardized way, and to use this information to improve the safety and usability of robots in collaboration with humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantified injury potential of a collaborative robot design or system is an essential component in the overall risk assessment.
a collaborative robot system is safe for a given application scenario, if the injury potential of all foreseeable hazards is below a certain threshold.
a classification scheme and a standardized way to assess the injury potential are necessary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the injury potential of a robot can be quantified and that this information can be used for the design of safe robots.

we developed a classification scheme for holding information about the low-level injury risk of robots and we demonstrated that this classification scheme can be used to compare different collaborative robot designs.
we have developed and demonstrated the first injury risk quantification method that is suitable for industrial robots in collaborative operation with humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the classification scheme presented can be used to provide a common basis for communication and assessment between robot designers and end users, and can serve as a foundation for a future standard.
a well-founded understanding and classification of injury potential is essential for a successful deployment of human-safe robots.
a classification scheme for quantifying low-level injuries is needed to support the design and evaluation of collaborative robots.
